evidence.source: Feel Layer research, 8-9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest)

items.title: A new picture state every few seconds, without overload
items.summary: The picture changes every 2-4 seconds in long videos and every 1-2 seconds in Shorts. Never overload: no fast cut plus a new fact plus an intensity jump inside the same 2 seconds.

items.title: No frame may read as a still photo
items.summary: No stretch of the video may look like a still photo: every still gets parallax or particles, and the result is measured after render.

items.title: Characters blink, breathe and talk
items.summary: Character shots blink, breathe and move their mouths with the words. A reaction cutaway always shows the approved character art.

items.title: Sound and motion start in frame 1
items.summary: Motion starts within 0.1 seconds and sound within 0.2 seconds, with a 'you' question inside the first second. A silent or static first frame loses the viewer before the hook.

items.title: Pause, then punch
items.summary: 300-700 milliseconds of silence come before every punchline: the pause is what makes the line land.

items.title: Laugh density, chosen by a joke tournament
items.summary: A real punchline at least every 15 seconds in long videos and every 6 seconds in Shorts. Jokes come from a tournament of 20-40 candidates that strong judges see in full; the punch word comes last.

items.title: One send moment and one awe peak per video
items.summary: Every video holds one 'that is so you' moment worth sending to a friend and one awe peak. No sadness peak in the last 20% of the runtime.

items.title: Sound effects rotate before the ear gets used to them
items.summary: A listener habituates to a sound effect by its third repeat: no effect repeats within 3 uses or within 20 seconds, and story sounds (gavel, paper, fizzle) come in fresh variants.

items.title: Change the voice at least every 8 seconds
items.summary: A change of speaker at least every 8 seconds resists habituation better than any effect. Captions are kinetic and synced to the spoken word.

items.title: No near-copy of the last 10 videos
items.summary: No video may be a near-copy of any of the last 10: the ordered sequence of event types is compared, and a match sends the piece back.

items.title: Flash safety and caption safe zone
items.summary: At most 3 luminance flips a second anywhere in the video, and captions stay inside the safe zone of the frame.

items.title: ASMR textures are touches, never hooks
items.summary: ASMR-like textures please a minority of viewers: use them as short touches inside scenes, matched to the picture, and never in the hook.

evidence.source: Spin-off and sound research, 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest)

items.title: Loudness: -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP
items.summary: Every master is mixed to -14 LUFS with a true peak of -1 dBTP, so the video is neither turned down by the platform nor quieter than what plays before it.

evidence.source: Spin-off and sound research, 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest)

items.title: Sound effects only from licence-safe libraries
items.summary: Sound effects come only from licence-safe sources: the Sonniss GDC bundles, Kenney CC0, Freesound CC0 and the YouTube audio library.

evidence.source: Spin-off and sound research, 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest)

items.title: Depth maps for parallax: Depth Anything V2 Small
items.summary: Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0 licence) produces the depth maps that turn a still into a parallax shot at no per-use cost.
